summary_1line: Bhishma argues that preserving life and ruling wisely require flexible judgment, as righteousness and unrighteousness can appear in each other’s form.

image_candidates.scene_text: Viswamitra, gaunt from famine, cooks a haunch of dog's meat over a ritual fire while offering portions to the gods under a dark rain-filled sky.
Indra pours heavy rain from the heavens as parched earth below begins sprouting fresh green plants around the sacrificial fire.
The aged Bhishma lies on his bed of arrows instructing a troubled Yudhishthira about the confusing nature of righteousness and unrighteousness.
